verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Joel, son of Pethuel.
verses.1:2: Hear this, elders, and take it in with your ears, all inhabitants of the land: has this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
verses.1:3: Tell of this to your children, and let your children tell it to their children, and their children to another generation.
verses.1:4: What remained from the caterpillar, the locust has eaten; and what remained from the locust, the wingless locust has eaten; and what remained from the wingless locust, the blight has eaten.
verses.1:5: Wake up, drunkards, and weep and wail, all you who drink wine in sweetness, because it has perished from your mouth.
verses.1:6: For a nation has come up against My land, mighty and innumerable; its teeth are like the teeth of a lion, and its molars like those of a lion cub.
verses.1:7: It has turned My vine into a wasteland and peeled the bark from My fig tree; laying it bare, it has stripped it and flung it aside; its branches have become white.
verses.1:8: Lament like a virgin wrapped in sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
verses.1:9: Sacrifice and drink offering have perished from the house of the Lord; the priests, the ministers of the Lord, have mourned.
verses.1:10: The countryside has been ravaged, the ground has mourned, because the wheat has been devastated, the wine has been put to shame, the oil has languished.
verses.1:11: The farmers have been put to shame, the vinedressers have wailed over the grain and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
verses.1:12: The vine has been put to shame, and the fig tree has languished; the pomegranate, and the palm, and the apple tree, and all the trees of the field have dried up, because joy has been put to shame away from the sons of men.
verses.1:13: Gird yourselves and lament, priests; wail, ministers of the altar; go in, lie down in sackcloth, ministers of my God, since sacrifice and drink offering have vanished from the house of your God.
verses.1:14: Sanctify a fast, call an assembly, gather the elders, all the inhabitants of the land, into the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord.
verses.1:15: Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the day of the Lord is near, and it will come like devastation from the Mighty One.
verses.1:16: Have not provisions perished before your eyes from the house of our God, gladness and exultation?
verses.1:17: The beasts of burden have rotted in their dung; the granaries have been demolished, the storehouses have been broken down, because the wheat has been put to shame.
verses.1:18: Why did the beast groan, and the herds of cattle bellow? Because there is no pasture for them; and even the flocks of sheep have utterly perished.
verses.1:19: To You, Lord, I will cry out, because fire has consumed the lovely places of the wilderness, and flame has set ablaze all the trees of the countryside.
verses.1:20: Even the beasts of the field, like a plot of ground thirsting for rain, have looked up to You, because the springs of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the lovely places of the wilderness.
verses.2:1: Sound the trumpet in Zion, wail on My holy mountain; let all the inhabitants of the land be thrown into turmoil, because the day of the Lord is coming, because it is near.
verses.2:2: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and whirlwind: like the morning spread out over the mountains, a numerous and mighty people; there has not been one like it from the beginning, and after it there will not be, even to the years of generation and generation.
verses.2:3: Before its face is a devouring fire, and behind it a scorching flame. Like a garden of delight is the land before it, and behind it the desolation of a wilderness, and there is no one who escapes it.
verses.2:4: Like the appearance of horses is their appearance; and like horsemen, so they will run.
verses.2:5: Like the sound of chariots they will leap over the tops of the mountains, like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people prepared for battle.
verses.2:6: Before its face the peoples will be tormented; all faces will be reduced to a pot.
verses.2:7: Like mighty men they will run; like fighting men they will climb the wall; the men will march in their own ways, and they will not turn aside from their paths.
verses.2:8: No one will crowd his brother; each will walk in his own track; and they will even fall through the windows, and they will not be destroyed.
verses.2:9: They will enter the city, they will run along the wall, they will climb the houses, they will come in through the windows like a thief.
verses.2:10: Before its face the earth has trembled, the heavens have been shaken, the sun and the moon have been darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness.
verses.2:11: And the Lord has uttered His voice before the face of His army, because His camps are exceedingly numerous, because they are mighty and carry out His word; for the day of the Lord is great and very terrifying, and who will endure it?
verses.2:12: "Now therefore," says the Lord, "turn back to Me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in lamentation."
verses.2:13: And tear your hearts, and not your garments, and turn back to the Lord your God, because He is kind and merciful, patient and of great mercy, and ready to relent over calamity.
verses.2:14: Who knows whether He may turn back and pardon, and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord your God?
verses.2:15: Sound the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call an assembly.
verses.2:16: Gather the people, sanctify the assembly, bring together the elders, gather the little children and those nursing at the breast; let the bridegroom go out from his bedroom, and the bride from her bridal chamber.
verses.2:17: Between the vestibule and the altar the priests, the ministers of the Lord, will weep, and they will say, "Spare, Lord, spare Your people, and do not give Your inheritance to reproach, that the nations should rule over them. Why do they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.2:18: The Lord has become zealous for His land, and He has spared His people.
verses.2:19: And the Lord answered and said to His people, "Look, I will send you grain, and wine, and oil, and you will be filled with them; and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.
verses.2:20: And the one who is from the north I will put far away from you, and I will drive him out into a pathless and deserted land, his front toward the eastern sea and his rear toward the farthest sea; and his stench will rise, and his rot will rise, because he has acted proudly."
verses.2:21: Do not be afraid, land; exult and be glad, because the Lord has done great things.
verses.2:22: Do not be afraid, animals of the countryside, because the lovely places of the wilderness have sprouted, because the tree has borne its fruit; the fig tree and the vine have given their strength.
verses.2:23: And, children of Zion, exult and be glad in the Lord your God, because He has given you a teacher of righteousness, and He will cause the morning and evening rain to come down to you, as in the beginning.
verses.2:24: And the threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the presses will overflow with wine and oil.
verses.2:25: And I will restore to you the years that the locust, the wingless locust, and the blight, and the caterpillar have eaten, My great force that I sent against you.
verses.2:26: And eating, you will eat, and you will be satisfied; and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders with you; and My people will not be put to shame forever.
verses.2:27: And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Lord your God, and there is no other; and My people will not be put to shame for eternity.
verses.2:28: And it will happen after these things: I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
verses.2:29: And even on My male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out My Spirit.
verses.2:30: And I will give portents in heaven and on earth: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke.
verses.2:31: The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the day of the Lord comes, great and dreadful.
verses.2:32: And it will happen: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, because on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be salvation, just as the Lord has said, and among those who remain whom the Lord will call.
verses.3:1: For look, in those days and at that time, when I reverse the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.3:2: I will gather all the nations and lead them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will contend with them there over My people and My inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and they divided My land.
verses.3:3: And they cast a lot over My people; and they placed a boy in a brothel, and sold a girl for wine so that they might drink.
verses.3:4: Yet what is there between Me and you, Tyre and Sidon, and all the territory of the Philistines? Will you really pay back vengeance to Me? And if you avenge yourselves against Me, quickly, swiftly I will pay back recompense to you upon your head.
verses.3:5: For you took My silver and gold, and you brought My desirable and most beautiful things into your shrines.
verses.3:6: And you sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so that you might put them far away from their borders.
verses.3:7: Look, I will rouse them from the place in which you sold them, and I will turn back your retribution onto your head.
verses.3:8: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a faraway nation, for the Lord has spoken.
verses.3:9: Cry this out among the nations: sanctify war, rouse the mighty ones; let all the men of war approach, let them go up.
verses.3:10: Cut your plows into swords, and your hoes into spears. Let the weak one say, "I am strong."
verses.3:11: Burst forth and come, all nations from every side, and gather together; there the Lord will cause your mighty ones to fall.
verses.3:12: Let the nations rise and go up into the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations on every side.
verses.3:13: Thrust in the sickles, because the harvest has ripened; come and go down, for the winepress is full, the winepresses overflow; for their wickedness has been multiplied.
verses.3:14: Peoples, peoples, in the valley of cutting down, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of cutting down.
verses.3:15: The sun and the moon have been darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness.
verses.3:16: And the Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem He will utter His voice, and the heavens and the earth will be shaken; and the Lord is the hope of His people and the strength of the sons of Israel.
verses.3:17: And you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, My holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will not pass through her anymore.
verses.3:18: And it will be in that day: the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and waters will run through all the streams of Judah; and a spring will go out from the house of the Lord and water the torrent of thorns.
verses.3:19: Egypt will become a desolation, and Idumea a wilderness of destruction, because they acted unjustly against the sons of Judah and shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.3:20: And Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generation after generation.
verses.3:21: And I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed; and the Lord will dwell in Zion.

notes.1:4: Latin lists four crop destroyers: eruca ("caterpillar"), locusta ("locust"), bruchus ("wingless locust"), and rubigo ("blight" or mildew/rust, following the Septuagint rather than a fourth insect species as in the Hebrew).
notes.1:10: Latin confusum est literally means "has been put to shame" (or "confounded"), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew verb as "be ashamed" rather than "dry up." This Vulgate motif recurs in 1:11, 1:12, and 1:17 and is reversed in 2:26-27.
notes.1:11: The Vulgate renders these verbs as declarative perfects ("have been put to shame... have wailed") rather than imperatives as in the Hebrew text.
notes.1:17: Latin Computruerunt jumenta in stercore suo ("The beasts of burden have rotted in their dung") is a distinctively Vulgate rendering of a difficult Hebrew line usually understood as seeds shriveling beneath clods.
notes.1:20: The simile quasi area sitiens imbrem ("like a plot of ground thirsting for rain") is a Vulgate expansion rendering the Hebrew verb for panting or longing; likewise speciosa deserti ("lovely places of the wilderness," also in 1:19 and 2:22) reads the Hebrew word for "pastures" from the root meaning "lovely."
notes.2:3: Latin hortus voluptatis ("garden of delight") translates the meaning of Hebrew "garden of Eden," as voluptatis also does in Genesis 2:8 (paradisum voluptatis).
notes.2:6: Latin redigentur in ollam literally means "will be reduced to a pot," taking the rare Hebrew term parur as "cooking pot" (suggesting faces blackened like a soot-covered pot) rather than growing pale.
notes.2:8: Latin per fenestras cadent, et non demolientur ("fall through the windows, and they will not be destroyed") is a Vulgate-distinct reading; the Hebrew text speaks of plunging through weapons without breaking ranks.
notes.2:13: Latin praestabilis super malitia is a distinctive Vulgate idiom meaning "ready to relent over calamity," rendering Hebrew "relenting of disaster."
notes.2:23: Latin doctorem justitiae ("a teacher of righteousness") reads Hebrew moreh as "teacher" rather than "early rain"; imbrem matutinum et serotinum (lit. "morning and evening rain") denotes the early autumn and late spring rains.
notes.2:28: Native Clementine Vulgate Joel uses the three-chapter division (2:28-32 = Saints.Bible 3:1-5; 3:1-21 = Saints.Bible 4:1-21).
notes.2:29: Latin servos meos ("My male servants") includes the possessive "My" (agreeing with the Septuagint and Acts 2:18), whereas the Hebrew text reads simply "the male servants." Native Clementine Vulgate Joel 2:28-32 maps to Saints.Bible 3:1-5 and native 3:1-21 maps to Saints.Bible 4:1-21.
notes.2:30: Latin vaporem fumi ("vapor of smoke") follows the Septuagint rather than Hebrew "columns of smoke."
notes.3:11: Vulgate "ibi occumbere faciet Dominus robustos tuos" makes the Lord the subject of a future threat of defeat against the enemy's warriors ("cause your mighty ones to fall"), whereas the Hebrew is commonly read as a prayer asking the Lord to bring down His own mighty ones.
notes.3:14: Vulgate reads "Populi, populi, in valle concisionis" ("Peoples, peoples, in the valley of cutting down"), taking the Hebrew term (which can mean "decision") as an act of cutting down or slaughter.
notes.3:18: Vulgate "dulcedinem" ("sweetness") and "torrentem spinarum" ("torrent of thorns") render the Hebrew terms for "sweet wine" and the place-name "Valley of Shittim" (acacias) literally.
notes.3:19: Latin "Idumaea" ("Idumea") is the Greco-Latin territorial name corresponding to Hebrew "Edom," just as "Judaea" ("Judea") in 4:20 corresponds to Hebrew "Judah."
notes.3:21: Vulgate "mundabo sanguinem eorum, quem non mundaveram" ("I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed") renders the debated Hebrew verb literally as purification rather than "avenge" or "acquit."
